mcq.q: The overall design of a database is called the ______, while the data stored at a given point of time is the ______.
mcq.e: Schema is the design; instance is the state (data) at a moment in time.

mcq.q: Metadata, i.e. data about data, is kept in the:
mcq.e: The data catalog (data dictionary) is the system database describing the data.

mcq.q: Which is the OLDEST of these database models?
mcq.e: Hierarchical came first, then network, relational and object-oriented.

mcq.q: A filing cabinet holding a folder for each customer is an example of which data model?
mcq.e: The customer-folder filing cabinet is the standard hierarchical example.

mcq.q: Which of the following is NOT a category of DBMS?
mcq.e: Sequential is a file organisation, not a DBMS type.

mcq.q: Which of the following is NOT a database design approach?
mcq.e: The approaches are top-down, bottom-up and inside-out; there is no up-down.

mcq.q: The deductive database model is also known as the:
mcq.e: Deductive = inference model.

mcq.q: In the three-level architecture, which level describes the physical storage of data on disk?
mcq.e: Internal = physical storage; conceptual = logical design of whole database; external = user views.

mcq.q: Logical data independence means the ability to change the ______ schema without changing the ______ schemas.
mcq.e: Conceptual changes are hidden from user views (external schemas).

mcq.q: Which is NOT a feature or function of a DBMS?
mcq.e: A DBMS is built for many users, so single-user-only access is not a feature.

mcq.q: Which of the following is NOT an element of a database?
mcq.e: Database elements are schema, relationships and constraints, not the frontend.

mcq.q: Deliberately increasing redundancy in a database to improve performance is called:
mcq.e: Denormalization walks back down the normal forms for speed.

mcq.q: Which is a tested disadvantage of a distributed database?
mcq.e: Distributed databases may suffer data inconsistency.

mcq.q: In a distributed database, breaking the database into logical units for the sites is called:
mcq.e: Fragmentation splits the DB into logical units; allocation decides which site stores what.

mcq.q: In a data warehouse environment, the intermediate stop of the ETL process is the:
mcq.e: The staging area is the ETL intermediate store.

mcq.q: A star schema consists of:
o: One central fact table plus one table per dimension
Two fact tables linked by a key
mcq.e: Star schema = one fact table surrounded by dimension tables.

mcq.q: A relation has 50 tuples and 20 attributes. Its degree and cardinality are:
mcq.e: Degree = number of attributes (20); cardinality = number of tuples (50).

mcq.q: Table STUDENT has degree 20 and cardinality 300; TEACHER has degree 10 and cardinality 25. The Cartesian product has degree and cardinality:
mcq.e: Degrees add (20+10=30), cardinalities multiply (300x25=7500).

mcq.q: A table of degree 4 and cardinality 3 gets 3 more attributes and 4 more tuples. Its new degree and cardinality are:
mcq.e: Degree 4+3=7; cardinality 3+4=7.

mcq.q: Natural join of R (3 tuples) and S (2 tuples) can give at most how many tuples?
mcq.e: At most |R| x |S| = 6.

mcq.q: Which operation needs two tables that share a common column?
mcq.e: A join requires a common column; Cartesian product does not.

mcq.q: Which statement about set operations is correct?
o: Intersection is both commutative and associative
Intersection is neither commutative nor associative
mcq.e: Intersection is commutative and associative; difference is neither.

mcq.q: In an ER diagram, a double rectangle represents:
mcq.e: Double box = weak entity; double diamond = identifying relationship.

mcq.q: The partial key of a weak entity set is called the:
mcq.e: Discriminator + owner's PK forms the full key.

mcq.q: In an ER diagram, a dashed ellipse represents a ______ attribute.
mcq.e: Dashed ellipse = derived attribute, e.g. age from date of birth.

mcq.q: The degree of a relationship in the ER model is the number of:
mcq.e: Degree = number of participating entity types.

mcq.q: The top-down division of a higher-level entity set into sub-entity sets is called:
mcq.e: Specialisation is top-down; generalisation is bottom-up.

mcq.q: A candidate key is best described as a:
mcq.e: Candidate key = minimal superkey; a superkey need not be minimal.

mcq.q: Which statement about keys is correct?
o: A table can have only one primary key but multiple foreign keys
A table can have several primary keys
A superkey must always be minimal
A table can have only one foreign key
mcq.e: One PK (maybe composite), but many secondary and foreign keys.

mcq.q: The column that points to the primary key of another table and links tables is the:
mcq.e: The foreign key links tables.

mcq.q: Referential integrity between R1 (parent) and R2 (child) can be violated by:
o: INSERT into R2 and DELETE from R1
INSERT into R1 and DELETE from R2
mcq.e: Inserting into the child or deleting from the parent can leave dangling FK values.

mcq.q: Entity integrity states that:
o: No primary key value can be NULL
Every foreign key must be NULL
Every table must have a foreign key
mcq.e: Entity integrity pairs with the primary key; referential integrity with the foreign key.

mcq.q: Which is NOT an SQL constraint?
mcq.e: UNION is a set operator.

mcq.q: In a functional dependency X -> Y, X is called the:
mcq.e: Left side is the determinant, right side the dependent.

mcq.q: Which is NOT a primary Armstrong's axiom?
mcq.e: Pseudo-transitivity is a derived rule.

mcq.q: Given F = {P->RT, Q->S, R->PS, QS->TU}, the closure of PQ is:
mcq.e: P gives R,T; Q gives S; QS gives U; so every attribute is included.

mcq.q: Second Normal Form (2NF) removes:
mcq.e: 2NF needs full functional dependence on the whole primary key.

mcq.q: Which normal form is considered adequate/satisfactory for normal RDBMS design?
mcq.e: 3NF is the adequate form for practical design.

mcq.q: A relation is in BCNF if, whenever a non-trivial FD X -> A holds:
o: X is a candidate key attribute only
mcq.e: BCNF: every determinant is a superkey.

mcq.q: Which is a DDL command?
mcq.e: DDL = CREATE, ALTER, DROP, TRUNCATE; UPDATE and INSERT are DML.

mcq.q: Which command belongs to DCL?
mcq.e: DCL = GRANT and REVOKE.

mcq.q: Which statement adds a column FEES to table TEACHER?
o: ALTER TABLE TEACHER ADD COLUMN FEES FLOAT;
MODIFY TABLE TEACHER ADD FEES FLOAT;
EDIT TABLE TEACHER ADD FEES FLOAT;
UPDATE TABLE TEACHER ADD FEES FLOAT;
mcq.e: ALTER TABLE adds, deletes or modifies columns; MODIFY/EDIT TABLE do not exist.

mcq.q: Which statement is TRUE about TRUNCATE TABLE?
o: It removes all rows quickly, is DDL and is faster than DELETE
It is DML and can be rolled back like DELETE
It removes the table structure too
It deletes only rows matching a WHERE clause
mcq.e: TRUNCATE keeps the structure, removes all rows fast, and is DDL.

mcq.q: ROLLBACK to a savepoint does NOT:
o: Erase all modifications from the start of the transaction
Erase savepoints created after the target
mcq.e: Erasing everything from the start is a full ROLLBACK; savepoint rollback keeps the target and later savepoints are erased.

mcq.q: Which SQL statement increases every student's fees by 10 percent?
mcq.e: UPDATE ... SET is the SQL form; MODIFY/CHANGE/ASSIGN are not SQL.

mcq.q: The logical evaluation order of a SELECT query is:
o: FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, SELECT, ORDER BY
SELECT, FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY
FROM, SELECT, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY
WHERE, FROM, GROUP BY, SELECT, HAVING, ORDER BY
mcq.e: Written order starts with SELECT, but evaluation begins at FROM and SELECT comes after HAVING.

mcq.q: Which clause filters groups after GROUP BY has formed them?
mcq.e: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups.

mcq.q: Which pattern retrieves values that contain the text INDIA anywhere?
mcq.e: % matches any run of characters; _ matches exactly one.

mcq.q: Which query correctly finds rows where Address has no value?
mcq.e: Nothing equals NULL; use IS NULL.

mcq.q: What does ORDER BY title, name DESC do?
o: Titles ascending; names within each title descending
mcq.e: Each column carries its own direction; ASC is the default.

mcq.q: Which join returns all rows from both tables, with NULLs for non-matches?
mcq.e: FULL JOIN keeps unmatched rows of both sides.

mcq.q: A view in SQL is best described as a:
o: Virtual table derived from other tables
mcq.e: A view stores no real rows; the base table does.

mcq.q: WITH CHECK OPTION on a view ensures that:
o: Inserted or updated rows satisfy the view's WHERE clause
mcq.e: It forces writes through the view to satisfy its WHERE condition.

mcq.q: Among Minus, Intersect, Union and Count, which is an aggregate function?
mcq.e: The others are set operators.

mcq.q: A table has column GAME values (x, y, z, NULL) and SALARY 60000, 80000, NULL. COUNT(GAME) and AVG(SALARY) are:
mcq.e: Column counts and AVG skip NULLs: AVG = (60000+80000)/2.

mcq.q: ROUND(65.726, -1) returns:
mcq.e: Negative precision rounds to tens, giving 70.

mcq.q: Which operator concatenates strings in standard SQL?
mcq.e: || is concatenation.

mcq.q: Which of these is NOT a valid SQL:1999 data type?
mcq.e: ENUM is MySQL-only.

mcq.q: Valid SQL comment styles are:
mcq.e: // is not valid SQL.

mcq.q: Which is NOT a member of ACID?
mcq.e: ACID = Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability.

mcq.q: Which is NOT a timestamp-ordering variant?
mcq.e: Variants are total, partial and multiversion.

mcq.q: In two-phase locking, lock requests occur in the ______ phase and unlocks in the ______ phase.
mcq.e: 2PL has a growing then a shrinking phase.

mcq.q: A lost update occurs when:
o: Both transactions read X and then both write X
mcq.e: The R1 R2 W1 W2 trace loses one write. Reading uncommitted data is a dirty read.

mcq.q: Reading data written by an uncommitted transaction is called a:
mcq.e: Dirty read = reading uncommitted data.

mcq.q: Conflict serializability of a schedule is tested using a:
mcq.e: If the precedence graph is acyclic, the schedule is conflict serializable.

mcq.q: A checkpoint is the synchronisation point between:
mcq.e: It limits the recovery work after a crash.

mcq.q: Which deadlock-prevention scheme is preemptive?
mcq.e: Wait-die is non-preemptive; wound-wait is preemptive.

mcq.q: Which index is best suited for range queries?
mcq.e: B-tree = ranges; hash = exact match.

mcq.q: DEFRAGMENTATION refers to:
o: Relocating small non-contiguous disk blocks into contiguous ones
mcq.e: Do not confuse with data fragmentation in distributed databases.

mcq.q: ISAM stands for:
mcq.e: ISAM = Indexed Sequential Access Method.

tf.s: The instance of a database is its overall design.
tf.n: The schema is the design; the instance is the state at a point in time.

tf.s: Hierarchical is the oldest data model, followed by network and relational.
In a relation, degree is the number of tuples and cardinality is the number of attributes.
A superkey must always be a minimal set of attributes.
tf.n: Minimality is required for a candidate key, not a superkey.

tf.s: Nulls reduce the space requirement of an RDBMS.
A weak entity is drawn with a double rectangle.
tf.n: Its identifying relationship is a double diamond.

tf.s: Higher normal forms mean less redundancy.
tf.n: 4NF is more immune to inconsistencies than 3NF.

tf.s: UPDATE and INSERT are DDL commands.
tf.n: They are DML; DDL = CREATE, ALTER, DROP, TRUNCATE.

tf.s: HAVING needs GROUP BY, and HAVING executes before WHERE.
tf.n: HAVING works with GROUP BY, but runs after WHERE.
BETWEEN is inclusive at both ends.

tf.s: NULL <= NULL evaluates to TRUE in SQL.
tf.n: It evaluates to UNKNOWN; only NULL IS NULL is TRUE.

tf.s: A SQL:1999 view definition may use ORDER BY.
tf.n: Views may use subqueries and aggregates but not ORDER BY.

tf.s: An exclusive lock allows both reading and writing.
tf.n: Shared lock = read only; exclusive = read and write.

tf.s: DROP TABLE removes both the data and the structure of the table.
tf.n: DELETE removes only rows; DROP removes the table itself.

fill.q: The database language used by MySQL, Informix and SQL Server is ______.
CRUD stands for Create, Read, Update and ______.
The ER-model term for the partial key of a weak entity set is the ______.
The SQL command used to give access rights, e.g. SELECT on Customers to a user, is ______.
The DDL command that removes all rows quickly but keeps the table structure is ______.
The default sort order of ORDER BY is ______ (ascending/descending).
The SQL keyword that makes the changes of a transaction permanent is ______.
A shared lock allows a transaction to only ______ the data item.
A database design approach in which design starts from the whole and goes down to details is called ______-down.
In two-phase locking, the phase in which locks are released is called the ______ phase.
The ER-model term for treating a relationship as an entity is ______.
The data warehouse is used for ______ (analysis), whereas operational databases are used for OLTP.
The SQL join of a table with itself is called a ______ join.
